_readme: Every number this card runs on. The scripts read it; nothing is typed twice.
model_state.py carries a fallback copy of all of it, so a broken or missing
file cannot cost a card. When it falls back, the card says so.
WHAT IS MEASURED AND WHAT IS CHOSEN:
the preseason conversion is measured, on 352 team-seasons. Nothing under
'grading' is. This card has no backtest yet, so every grading value is a
decision somebody made, not a finding, and the letters on the card are claims
no record stands behind. The college card grades on the same scheme and had to
cap it, because run unchanged there it graded most of a slate A on a strategy
that backtested below break-even. Filling in 'backtest' below is the next work.
WHERE TEAMS START:
preseason.mode is 'market', so a team's Week 1 rating is the sportsbook season
win total in preseason_2026.csv, converted to points. Set it to 'last_season'
to go back to last year's play-by-play regressed toward the mean.
STILL TO DO, ratings.seasons:
the play-by-play fit still sees 2025 only, so once 2026 games are played there
is nothing that lets them into the ratings. How fast results should take over
from the preseason number is a number that has to be measured, not picked, and
that needs the backtest. Until then the card sits on the market's preseason view.
The staleness check in nfl_card.py cannot catch that. It compares the
modification time of power_ratings.csv, and the Tuesday rebuild rewrites that
file every week, so it stays permanently fresh while the data underneath is a
season old. A check that cannot fail is not a check.
